title: WPMS/1701/2013 of Tokeer Ahmad Vs Oriental Bank Of Commerce AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1701 of 2013 (M/S)
Tokeer Ahmad. ........Petitioner
 Versus
Oriental Bank of Commerce
and others. .......Respondents
Mr. G.S. Negi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate for respondent no.1/Bank.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Dated: July 24, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
 Present petition has been filed by the petitioner
challenging the recovery citation dated 08.07.2013 issued
by respondent no.3 for recovery of ` 1,17,655/-. Further
prayer has been made seeking directions to the
respondents not to take any coercive measures against the
petitioner in pursuance of recovery citation. The
petitioner has sought further directions to the
respondent/ Bank to permit the petitioner to deposit `
1,06,959/- in the Bank within a period of one year.
 According to the petitioner, limit of ` 1,00,000/-
was sanctioned to the petitioner by the respondent
no.1/Bank for commercial purpose to run a small
hardware shop. The petitioner deposited some amount,
but due to dullness in the business, he could not deposit
the limit except interest. It is submitted that the petitioner
is a poor person and recovery of a huge amount is being
made against him as arrears of land revenue.

2
 Mr. G.S. Negi, Advocate for the petitioner prayed
that the petitioner is not getting sufficient earning to
repay the huge amount in lump sum. He submitted that
the respondent no.3 has issued the Recovery Citation by
which a sum of ` 1,17,655/- is sought to be recovered
from the petitioner. He further submitted that the
petitioner is ready to deposit the outstanding balance
amount of loan limit in easy installments fixed by this
Court until and unless the entire amount is deposited. Mr.
Ashish Joshi, Advocate appearing for the Bank submitted
that, in case, petitioner is accommodated to deposit the
loan amount in installments, directions may be issued to
deposit the same with interest alongwith the recovery
charges and also condition may be imposed that any
failure on the part of the petitioner, order passed by this
Court shall be vacated.
 Having heard learned counsel for the parties and by
consent of the parties, the writ petition is disposed of in
the following manner:-
(i) The impugned R.C. dated 08.07.2013 issued
by respondent no.3 is hereby quashed.
(ii) The petitioner is permitted to deposit the
outstanding sum of loan to the Bank in ten
monthly installments alongwith recovery
charges.
(iii) The first installment shall be paid by 15th of
August, 2013 and remaining 9 installments
shall be paid before 15th of each month.
(iv) Any failure on the part of the petitioner shall
amount to automatic vacation of the order.
 Stay application (CLMA No. 7594/2013) also stands
disposed of.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 24.07.2013
